why: The authors' repository is cloned and contains the R implementation plus the real datasets needed for Table 3 (Lymphoma) and Figure 7 (Usoskin/GSE59739). The match target C1 is produced by code_11_table3.R. The only likely fixes are environmental: installing R/Rcpp/Rtools and any undeclared R packages, not rebuilding the method or data.
missing_artifacts: Windows compilation toolchain for initcenters_oncepkpod_functions.cpp (Rtools) if Rcpp::sourceCpp is used
blockers_seen: Repository is R-based while the machine lists Python 3.12 and no R installation.
No dependency file is provided; R packages must be inferred from scripts and installed manually.
A C++ helper exists, so Rcpp and a compiler (Rtools on Windows) may be required.

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: About 10-20 minutes for R/Rtools/package setup if not already present; the C1 Table 3 row itself should take a few minutes for n=62, p=4026, k=3 and 10 repetitions. Full 20-minute budget is tight if toolchain installation is needed.
feasibility.scale_down_plan: Run only the C1 row (Lymphoma, k=3, MNAR0 30%) with 3-5 repetitions instead of 10, and if Rcpp compilation is problematic, port only the one-time center initialization helper to plain R. This gives a noisier CER estimate but preserves the proposed-vs-k-POD comparison.

compute.basis: C1 needs 10 repetitions of k=3 clustering on a 62 x 4026 matrix with 30% missingness and 5 lambda candidates; the numerical fits are small, while R/Rcpp environment setup and repeated R loops dominate command time.
